verdict.root_cause: A traffic-shaping (netem) sidecar attached to cartservice's network namespace ~3 minutes before onset applied a fixed 300 ms egress delay with zero jitter and was still in effect at incident time [tr_cb602d1af2c1]. Every cartservice Redis client span sits on a hard ~300 ms floor with near-zero handler self-time, so all elapsed time is waiting on egress-delayed cache calls [tr_a7d576a32ef6]. The penalty is charged per call, so checkoutservice accrues ~900 ms per cart call and its error ratio rose from ~1.7% to ~18.2% as calls exceeded deadlines [tr_6b7bfb1ca61f]. cartservice itself served traffic continuously with no crashes or dependency errors [tr_425aee5c5bc0]. The mechanism is induced wait on a dependency call path, not a broken artifact or a wrong endpoint value.
verdict.reasoning: The change record names a netem attach at 12:02 with delay=300ms jitter=0ms as the only change still active at onset, and rules out the hotfix image and REDIS_ADDR override as both reverted beforehand [tr_cb602d1af2c1]. Traces match that parameter numerically and structurally: a ~6 ms band above 300 ms, identical on reads and writes, repeating per outbound call, with sub-millisecond cartservice self-time — excluding queueing, CPU work, and write-path stalls [tr_a7d576a32ef6]. Checkout's error surge follows from multiplying that per-call penalty across several cart calls, while all non-cart checkout dependencies finish in 0-14 ms [tr_6b7bfb1ca61f, tr_a7d576a32ef6]. Logs confirm a live, non-restarting cartservice, eliminating crash-loop and startup-misconfiguration stories [tr_425aee5c5bc0]. Removing the shaping rule is the fix, hence config_revert.
open_questions: checkoutservice's error change point is at 11:43, ~19 minutes before the netem attach [tr_6b7bfb1ca61f]; an earlier chaos cycle or a separate contributing fault was never measured.
Trace coverage is only 12:06:45-12:07:14 and logs drop ~11:35-12:06:45 [tr_a7d576a32ef6, tr_425aee5c5bc0], so the delay's onset was inferred from parameter match, not observed.
No cartservice latency or request-rate series exists; the only metric attempted returned no samples in either window [tr_eb93ab5d8384], and whether the sidecar is still attached was not verified.

alternatives.root_cause: A separate fault at checkoutservice beginning ~11:43 drives the error surge, with cart latency only aggravating it.
alternatives.why_not: Traces attribute ~2.4 s of a 2.45 s checkout root to two cart calls while all other dependencies finish in 0-14 ms [tr_a7d576a32ef6].

alternatives.root_cause: The Redis cache backing cartservice slowed on its own, adding ~300 ms per operation.
alternatives.why_not: A loaded cache yields a right-skewed spread and read/write asymmetry; the observed floor is flat at exactly the injected 300 ms on both HGET and HMSET [tr_a7d576a32ef6, tr_cb602d1af2c1].

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed. The mechanism is an external netem sidecar attached to cartservice's network namespace [tr_cb602d1af2c1]; no permitted action removes it. revert_config would restore cartservice env/config, but no config or flag change on cartservice was in effect at onset (REDIS_ADDR was reverted ~3.2h earlier), so its precondition is not met. rollback_image is ruled out because the hotfix image was already reverted ~13m before onset. restart_service is wrong because the evidence points at a change, not process state, and logs show continuous healthy serving.
proposal.if_wrong: If change history actually records a cartservice configuration entry in the incident window that carries the shaping rule (i.e. the netem attach is modelled as config rather than a sibling container), revert_config on cartservice becomes viable and abstaining was too cautious. Confirmation would be Redis client spans dropping from the ~300 ms floor to single-digit ms after the revert.
proposal.risk: Abstaining leaves the 300 ms per-call egress delay in place, so checkoutservice keeps failing ~18% of calls and cart/checkout latency stays elevated until a human detaches the sidecar. Also leaves the unexplained 11:43 error change point [tr_6b7bfb1ca61f] uninvestigated.
proposal.blast_radius: No service is changed. Continued user-visible impact for frontend, checkoutservice and loadgenerator, which are the callers on the cart path; cartservice itself stays up.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Multiple services alerted near-simultaneously across the checkout path, not a single isolated warning, so this cannot be dismissed as noise. The fan-in pattern at cartservice/checkoutservice with frontend following suggests a shared downstream dependency slowdown.
